headlines.title: Could the Suspected Pneumonic Plague Case in Russia Lead to an Outbreak? Experts Weigh in
headlines.description: The death of a lab technician in Russia from suspected pneumonic plague has sparked global alarm. Could it lead to a bigger outbreak, or a pandemic? Experts explain.

headlines.title: U.S. monitors suspected Russian plague case as Trump plans call with Putin
headlines.description: Trump has said the U.S. is willing to help Russia, where the death of a staffer at an anti-plague lab has sparked global public health concerns.

headlines.title: Report finds discounts on Trump's drug website are hit or miss
headlines.description: As President Trump increasingly touts his "TrumpRx" drug website, a recent analysis shows the savings offered through the program are hit or miss. NBC News' Berkeley Lovelace has details on the potential savings offered through the website amid a slight dip in overall prices.

headlines.title: Ron Bennington Talks Hosting Comedy Podcast During Chemo
headlines.description: Comedian and radio host Ron Bennington, who is being treated for colorectal cancer, and Dr. Mark Pochapin, director of gastroenterology at NYU Langone Health and “Doctor Radio” on Sirius XM, join TODAY to discuss Bennington’s podcast that is spreading laughs and hope, and the importance of relationships on health. "Using humor is such an important vehicle...makes tough times able to endure," Dr. Pochapin says.

headlines.title: Meet the Woman Bringing 4th Trimester Care to American Moms
headlines.description: The first couple weeks after giving birth can be challenging for most new moms so one business owner in Chicago is on a mission to offer young families a different path. A doula by training, Taylor Michelle Ivey runs The Fourth Trimester focused on helping parents navigate those harried, often sleepless, first 12 weeks after childbirth at one of the only postpartum retreats in the United States. NBC’s Laura Jarrett reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Exclusive: Promising Brain Cancer Vaccine Gives Hope to Patients
headlines.description: Each year, some 15,000 Americans are diagnosed with glioblastoma, the deadliest form of brain cancer. Only 7% live more than five years but a new vaccine still in development could offer patients more time. NBC’s Anne Thompson reports for TODAY.

headlines.description: The death of a 28-year-old woman who worked in an anti-plague laboratory in Russia is raising concerns about what caused her illness.
